To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the guidelines are useful for designing experiments in conceptual modeling, (2) the guidelines are supported by empirical data, and (3) the guidelines are violated in some recent experimental work.

(a) experiments on conceptual modeling should be designed to evaluate representation fidelity, and (b) experiments that evaluate representation fidelity should use guidelines for experimental materials.

(1) a conceptual modeling technique that is not designed to facilitate the communication between users and analysts will fail to facilitate communication; (2) a conceptual modeling language that is not designed for the domain in question will be inadequate to represent domain knowledge; and (3) a conceptual modeling approach that does not provide a means of validating domain knowledge is not useful for conceptual modeling.

experiments that evaluate conceptualization techniques should be grounded in a theory of conceptual modeling and that the theory should be used to develop the experimental materials.
